narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and your job type. Your short nine-month loan request was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward approval. Most approved applicants ask for almost twice as long (19 months on average), so a brief duration normally signals lower risk. Unfortunately, two other important details worked against you and ultimately outweighed that positive signal.

Your checking account is currently in negative balance. Only about 13% of approved applicants are in the same situation, while nearly 60% have no checking account at all or a positive balance. This status pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit. In addition, although you hold a management or highly skilled position (a category shared by just 17% of applicants), the model interpreted this combination of factors as carrying higher risk than applicants in more common skilled-office roles.

Taken together, the negative influence from your account status and job category exceeded the reassuring effect of the short loan term, tipping the decision against approval.

You should focus on building a positive checking-account balance and, if possible, reapply later with a slightly longer but still manageable loan duration. This combination would likely improve your chances.
